source: Refreshed by daily scheduled task on 2026-05-01. Loved-list cross-check (Demon Slayer, Foundation, Severance, Black Mirror, Slow Horses, Good Omens, Rick and Morty) ran — no new continuations since yesterday's run; existing hero (Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle, on Crunchyroll since Apr 9) holds. Watchlist availability check ran — no new flips since yesterday; Widow's Bay, Your Friends & Neighbors S2, The Boys S5, Kevin, Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle all already streamable. New for May: La Brea S1–4 dropped on Netflix today (May 1); Citadel S2 confirmed May 6 (Prime); Good Omens S3 90-min finale confirmed May 13 (Prime); Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed confirmed May 20 (Apple TV+); Star City (For All Mankind expansion) confirmed May 29 (Apple TV+). Skips already-watched titles in watched.json and titles in not-interested.json. Hero remains Demon Slayer: Infinity Castle (Tier 1 Loved-list continuation + Tier 2 watchlist now-streaming).

hero.title: Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba — Infinity Castle
hero.about: First film in the trilogy adapting the Infinity Castle arc — the climactic showdown between the Demon Slayer Corps and Muzan's Upper Moons inside the shape-shifting fortress. Picks up directly from Hashira Training Arc. Made nearly $700M theatrically; Crunchyroll held it back from streaming until April 9, 2026 to protect the box office. Part 2 is confirmed for 2027 at the earliest, so this entry stands alone for now.
hero.why: Demon Slayer is on your Loved list — that's a higher-confidence signal than anything taste-extrapolated. Same studio (ufotable), same animation craft, an arc fans have been waiting years for. You pinned it; now it's actually on Crunchyroll. Tier 1 hero pick.

new_this_week.title: La Brea S1–4
new_this_week.about: Network sci-fi mystery (originally NBC, 2021–2024) — a massive sinkhole opens in Los Angeles, pulling people and buildings into a prehistoric land. Full four-season run dropped on Netflix today (May 1) as a binge-once package.
new_this_week.why: Sci-fi premise + world building + complete run (no future-season anxiety) checks three of your reward signals. Network-pacing means commercial-break beats — try one episode to see if the writing carries it past 'try.'

new_this_week.title: BEEF S2
new_this_week.about: Lee Sung Jin's Emmy-sweeping anthology resets with a brand-new cast and story: Oscar Isaac, Carey Mulligan, Charles Melton, Cailee Spaeny. Two couples at a Montecito beach club — the younger pair blackmails the older pair after catching them on video in a violent fight. Eight ~30-min episodes dropped at once. 86% RT and currently #2 on Netflix's global top 10.
new_this_week.why: S1 was praised for exactly the things you reward — dark humor, plot escalation, ensemble acting — and the anthology reset means no S1 baggage.

new_this_week.title: Apex
new_this_week.about: Charlize Theron plays Sasha, an experienced climber grieving the loss of her partner; alone in the Australian wilderness, what begins as endurance becomes a cat-and-mouse hunt with a methodical predator (Taron Egerton). Directed by Baltasar Kormákur. Eric Bana co-stars.
new_this_week.why: Pure survival thriller — strong premise but no off-beat humor or sci-fi/supernatural angle to push it past 'try.' Good if you specifically want a tense one-night watch.

new_this_week.title: The Four Seasons S2
new_this_week.about: Comedy-drama from Tina Fey, Lang Fisher, Tracey Wigfield. Three couples reunite for seasonal getaways. Ensemble led by Fey, Steve Carell, Will Forte, Colman Domingo. Tone: middle-aged friendship dynamics, sharp dialogue, brisk runtime.
new_this_week.why: Witty banter + ensemble cast hits two of your signals. Lower-stakes than your usual sweet spot, but Fey's writing room is reliable for one-and-done evening watches.

new_this_week.title: Lord of the Flies
new_this_week.about: BBC miniseries adaptation of William Golding's novel — boys stranded on an island, society breaks down. Faithful take with prestige-drama production.
new_this_week.why: Book adaptation is a positive signal for you; psychological pressure-cooker setup has plot-twist potential. Tonally darker than your usual — try one episode.

new_this_week.title: Widow's Bay
new_this_week.date: Apr 28 — now streaming, weekly through Jun 17
new_this_week.about: Matthew Rhys plays the mayor of Widow's Bay, a sleepy fictional New England island town that may or may not be cursed. Created by Katie Dippold (writer of The Heat and Spy, alum of Parks & Rec). Ten-episode first season — first two episodes premiered Apr 28; weekly Wednesdays through June 17 (special two-episode drop May 27). 100% Certified Fresh on Rotten Tomatoes (34 reviews); Metacritic 77/100.
new_this_week.why: On your watchlist and Certified Fresh out of the gate. Off-beat tone, supernatural premise, ensemble acting, plot-twist machinery. Dippold also wrote two of your 'Loved' list films (The Heat, Spy). Highest-priority try this week.

new_this_week.title: Your Friends & Neighbors S2
new_this_week.about: Jon Hamm returns as Coop, the financial-titan-turned-suburban-burglar. James Marsden joins this season and reviewers single him out as scene-stealing. Apple's #1 show globally on launch week. Glossy crime caper with ensemble dialogue, escalating consequences, dark comic streak.
new_this_week.why: On your watchlist. Strong critical reception, Hamm's best post-Mad Men work. Crime-comedy with witty banter and plot escalation is squarely in your strike zone.

new_this_week.title: Criminal Record S2
new_this_week.about: Peter Capaldi and Cush Jumbo return. After a young man is stabbed at a political rally, rival London detectives are forced into an uneasy alliance — what starts as a murder hunt escalates into an undercover operation against a far-right bomb plot. Eight episodes, one a week through June 10. 100% RT — higher than S1's already certified fresh 90%.
new_this_week.why: British police thriller with ensemble heavyweights, razor-sharp writing, escalating-plot machinery. Adjacent to the Slow Horses lane you 4⭐'d. Best critic-validated drop on Apple this month.

new_this_week.title: Outcome
new_this_week.about: Jonah Hill comedy-drama. Limited info available beyond the cast and platform; reviews mixed at best.
new_this_week.why: Hill comedy-drama isn't a strong taste-match given mixed signals. Skip unless you want a low-stakes one-night watch.

new_this_week.title: The Boys S5 (Final)
new_this_week.about: Final season, eight episodes, weekly Wednesdays through May 20. 95% RT through 55 reviews. Wraps up Homelander vs. Butcher. Garth Ennis source material; ensemble dark comedy with the show's usual escalation.
new_this_week.why: On your watchlist. Last-season urgency + dark satire + plot escalation aligns with your reward signals. The series has always been gross-out adjacent — pace yourself if that's a sticking point.

new_this_week.title: Kevin
new_this_week.about: Aubrey Plaza and Joe Wengert's animated series. Jason Schwartzman voices Kevin, a housecat who decides to try life without people; Plaza voices Dana, one of the humans he leaves behind. All 8 episodes dropped at once. Daily Beast called it 'hilariously filthy.' Star-studded guest cast.
new_this_week.why: On your watchlist. Adult animation + off-beat humor + 30-min episodes triple-stacks your signals — same pocket as Solar Opposites and Rick and Morty. Plaza's deadpan comedy DNA fits your dark-humor reward pattern.

new_this_week.title: The House of the Spirits
new_this_week.about: Eight-part adaptation of Isabel Allende's 1982 novel. Multi-generational saga of the Trueba family in Chile, blending political turmoil with magical realism. First three episodes premiered Apr 29; finale May 13. 80% RT. Told in Spanish with a Latin American/Spanish cast.
new_this_week.why: Book adaptation + supernatural elements hit positive signals; Spanish-language watch is also a Spanish-tutor side-benefit. Multi-generational drama is heavier than your typical pick — try the first episode.

new_this_week.title: Spider-Noir
new_this_week.about: Nicolas Cage stars as Ben Reilly, a 1930s private detective Spider-Man. Live-action take on the Spider-Verse Spider-Noir character. Eight episodes from Amazon MGM. Drops May 27.
new_this_week.why: Stylized noir setting + Cage's full-commit acting could play to the off-beat signal. No supernatural/sci-fi anchor though — flag for end of May.

new_this_week.title: Witch Hat Atelier
new_this_week.about: Long-awaited adaptation of Kamome Shirahama's manga. Coco, a young girl who dreams of becoming a witch, gets her chance after a chance encounter with a traveling magician. Heavy on world building and visual craft.
new_this_week.why: Fantasy anime with strong world building hits your sweet spot. Coming-of-age tone is lighter than your usual but the magic-system rigor scratches the same itch as Foundation/Sandman.

new_this_week.title: Dorohedoro S2
new_this_week.about: Long-delayed S2 of the cult-favorite manga adaptation. Caiman, a man with a reptile head and amnesia, hunts the sorcerer who cursed him. Vibe: gruesome but absurdly funny, with deep world building.
new_this_week.why: Dark humor + supernatural + off-beat — three of your strongest signals stacked. Body-horror visuals are gnarly but they're load-bearing for the comedy. Worth catching up on S1 if you didn't.

new_this_week.title: Chainsaw Man — The Movie: Reze Arc
new_this_week.about: First feature-length film in MAPPA's Chainsaw Man series. Adapts manga chapters 39–52 covering the entire Reze Arc — Denji's romance with a barista who is not what she seems. Premiered theatrically in Japan in Sept 2025; landed on Crunchyroll Apr 30 with both subbed and dubbed versions as part of Crunchyroll's Ani-May celebration.
new_this_week.why: Dark humor + supernatural + plot-twist machinery + MAPPA's animation craft — Chainsaw Man's tone is Demon-Slayer-adjacent with sharper teeth. Reze Arc is widely considered the best self-contained Chainsaw Man story; works as a standalone if you haven't watched the TV series.

new_this_week.title: Maximum Pleasure Guaranteed
new_this_week.date: May 20 — premieres with 2 eps, weekly through Jul 15
new_this_week.about: Darkly comedic thriller from creator David J. Rosen. Emmy winner Tatiana Maslany plays Paula, a newly divorced mom who falls down a dangerous rabbit hole of blackmail, murder, and youth soccer. 10 episodes, half-hour, premieres with two eps May 20 then weekly Wednesdays through July 15.
new_this_week.why: Dark comedy-thriller + 30-min episodes + Maslany's Orphan Black ensemble pedigree triple-stacks your reward signals. Premieres mid-month — flag now so it's on your radar when CDMX trip wraps.

critics.title: Criminal Record S2
critics.about: Capaldi/Jumbo British police thriller. 100% RT. See full entry above.
critics.why: Best critic-validated new drop on a service you have, and it's parked in your Slow Horses comfort zone.

critics.title: Widow's Bay
critics.about: Matthew Rhys-led comedy-horror, Katie Dippold creator. 100% RT (34 reviews) on debut.
critics.why: Critic darling that also happens to nail your taste profile. Same week's other watchlist title that just landed.

critics.title: How to Get to Heaven from Belfast
critics.about: Lisa McGee (Derry Girls) follow-up. RT consensus: 'triumphantly funny and proudly Irish.' Limited run.
critics.why: Witty + Irish + Lisa McGee. Light-tone-with-substance is one of your ten 'lands' signals — and the McGee writing room has a reliable hit rate.
